explanations: luna: The fire first illuminates its surroundings, then its light is taken away and people are left in darkness unable to see, a precise reversal of the fire that guides travelers. | terra: A kindled fire first lights its surroundings, then God removes their نُور and leaves them in darkness unable to see; the guiding function of fire is withdrawn before their eyes.
terra: After their fire-light is removed in 2:17, they are deaf, dumb, and blind and do not return; the sensory loss fixes their inability to retrace the route.
luna: This preceding ayah sets the thunderstorm, darkness, and lightning; 2:20 adds the people walking when its light appears, completing the wayfinding scene.
luna: When lightning illuminates the people, they walk by its light; when darkness returns, they stop. This closely parallels the section’s night traveler moving toward a visible fire.

luna: The section ends with people unable to leave the closed Fire; this ayah states that they cannot get out of the Fire (بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ). | terra: وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ states the final consequence of enclosure: there is no exit from the fire.
terra: God brings believers from darkness into light, while false patrons bring their followers from light into darkness and on to abiding in the Fire; direction is reversed into confinement.
terra: A fiery whirlwind strikes an aged person's fruit garden and burns it, a concrete Quranic parallel to destructive fire arriving upon cultivated security.
terra: Wealth and children cannot avail the disbelievers against God, and they become fuel for the Fire; presumed protection becomes the material of punishment.

luna: The section explicitly cites this wording as a secondary sense of ānastum (آنَسْتُم): guardians should see sound judgment in the orphans before returning property. It extends “noticing a fire” to recognizing maturity. | terra: فَإِنْ آنَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا is the section's other cited ء ن س formulation: perceiving maturity or right judgment clarifies how آنَسَ can mean discerning rather than social familiarity.
terra: Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly consume only fire into their bellies; misuse of wealth owed to the vulnerable is made fire before the final judgment.

terra: One who opposes the messenger after guidance is clear and follows another way is left to that choice and burned in Hell; route, following, rejected guidance, and fire form a single causal chain.

luna: This ayah announces a light (نُور) and a clear Book from God; 5:16 says what that light does as guidance. | terra: A light and clarifying Book are said to have come from God; 5:16 then states that God guides by it along paths of peace.

luna: The light leads its followers out of darkness into light and guides them to a straight path, matching the section’s beacon-as-guidance image. | terra: God guides those who seek His pleasure to paths of peace, brings them from darkness into light, and guides them to a straight path; light and routes perform the same guiding work as the section's beacon.
terra: They wish to leave the fire but وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا; this independently repeats the section's exitless, closed-fire claim.
luna: When night covers Abraham, he sees a star; this puts a visible light against night’s covering, like the section’s fire seen in darkness.
luna: The next ayah has Abraham see the moon and note that it sets; this plausibly extends the section’s night scene of a traveler seeing a light, though the moon here is not offered as a guide.

luna: The following ayah has Abraham see the sun and note that it sets; this plausibly extends the section’s seen-light scene, while its argument about created lights is not explicit in the fire passage.
luna: Abraham turns toward the Creator of the heavens and earth after the star, moon, and sun set; this continues 6:76–78 and complements the section’s question about who makes the fire.

luna: The night is made a rest (سَكَنًا) while sun and moon mark time; this is a related use of the section’s named s-k-n root, though the ayah assigns rest to night rather than fire. | terra: One ayah makes night سَكَنًا and sun and moon حُسْبَانًا; the section's lexicon separately calls a resting fire al-sakan and records destructive fire as a ḥusbān sense, so their ordinary cosmic meanings meet here.

luna: God makes the stars signs by which people find their way through the darkness of land and sea, a direct parallel to a high light serving a night traveler. | terra: God makes the stars so people may be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea, the Quran's clearest parallel to a night traveler steering by a distant elevated light.

luna: A person given light walks among people by it; this makes light a means of moving through the world, as in the section’s traveler following a fire. | terra: God gives one person a light with which he walks among people, while the other remains in darkness لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا; guiding light and exitless enclosure are set against each other.

luna: The ayah places a bed from Hell beneath them and coverings above them; this presents the punishment as surrounding them from both sides. | terra: Hell is a bed beneath them and coverings above them, لَهُم مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ, turning rest and shelter into total fiery confinement.
luna: The men on the heights recognize people by their marks across a barrier between Garden and Fire; this connects the section’s high-place signal and the two opposed destinies.
luna: The people on the heights turn their eyes toward the companions of the Fire and ask not to be placed with wrongdoers; it continues the boundary scene of 7:46.
luna: The men on the heights call to people they recognize and ask what their gathering and arrogance availed them; this ties the fire-bound scene to the section’s boast about heaps of wealth.
luna: The call turns to the people presumed unworthy of mercy and tells them to enter the Garden; it completes the split between the two groups in 7:46–48.
terra: يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ describes God covering day with night, supplying the actual covering action behind the source section's figurative k-f-r account of night.
luna: The people follow the light sent with the Messenger; this parallels the section’s beacon lit so travelers can follow it.
terra: Many destined for Hell have eyes with which they do not see; this makes refusal or failure to perceive the available sign a concrete antecedent of fire.
terra: Disbelievers spend wealth to block God's way, then suffer regret, defeat, and gathering into Hell; wealth used against the path ends in fire.
terra: Those who reject wish to extinguish God's نُور with their mouths, but God completes it; guiding light is treated as a flame opponents cannot put out.

luna: The warning addresses those who hoard gold and silver instead of spending in God’s way, directly linking the section’s amassed wealth to its fire. | terra: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way are warned of painful punishment, supplying the moral cause of the fire scene in 9:35.

luna: The next ayah says the hoarded metals will be heated in Hell and used to brand their foreheads, sides and backs; it gives a bodily punishment for the hoarding in 9:34. | terra: Hoarded treasure is heated in Hell's fire and brands foreheads, sides, and backs; accumulated wealth itself becomes the instrument of fire.
terra: أَلَا إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ directly makes encompassing Hell the boundary around those who cover or reject.
luna: The hypocrites avoid the heat of the expedition, but are told Hell’s fire is hotter; it reverses worldly avoidance of heat against the surah’s difficult path and the section’s final fire.
terra: The sun is radiance and the moon نُور, with measured stations for knowing years and حساب; illumination and the ح س ب field meet here in ordered reckoning rather than destructive ḥusbān.
terra: Faces are covered as if by pieces of dark night and their owners are companions of the Fire, joining night as covering directly to fiery confinement.

luna: The night is made for people to rest and the day visible; it joins the dictionary’s rest sense with the section’s night scene and fire’s visibility. | terra: God makes night for rest, لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ, and day for sight; the section's “resting fire” stands at the junction of those two ordinary functions.
terra: The ayah asks whether blind and seeing, or darknesses and light, can be equal, then challenges false creators; perception, illumination, and the true Creator are held together.

luna: The Book brings people from darkness to light and then to a path, an explicit light-and-way parallel to the section’s road beacon. | terra: The Book brings people from darknesses into light by God's permission and onto His path, explicitly joining illumination to route-guidance.
terra: Moses is commanded to bring his people from darknesses into light and remind them of God's days, joining his mission to illumination and remembrance.
terra: Their garments are pitch and fire covers their faces, تَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ; flame becomes an adhering cover rather than a visible point ahead.
terra: Hell has seven gates with an apportioned group for each, giving the punitive destination an explicit bounded architecture.

luna: This ayah says roads are made so people may be guided; it supplies the path that the landmarks and stars of 16:16 illuminate. | terra: God places roads in the earth لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ; the road itself is furnished for guidance just before signs and stars are named.

luna: The ayah names landmarks (عَلَٰمَٰتٍ) and stars as means of guidance, matching the section’s raised fire and road-sign. | terra: وَعَلَامَاتٍ وَبِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ joins road-marks and a high distant light as means of finding the way, closely matching the section's manār.

luna: The ayah makes night and day signs, effaces the night sign, and makes the day sign visible; it gives another specific account of light and darkness as alternating signs. | terra: God effaces the sign of night and makes the sign of day visible, distinguishing obscuring darkness from the light by which people seek their way and livelihood.
terra: The ayah opens with God's guidance and ends with Hell as the abode of those gathered blind, dumb, and deaf; failed sight and failed guidance terminate in fire.

luna: The fire’s enclosure surrounds the wrongdoers (أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا), a direct parallel to the sealed fire over people in the section. | terra: Hell's fire has a surrounding pavilion, أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا, and is called an evil resting place; it reverses both the open beacon and fire beside which one rests.
terra: The garden owner boasts of greater wealth and followers; this is the wealth-based confidence that the threatened ḥusbān of 18:40 will expose.
terra: He enters his garden wronging himself and assumes it will never perish, a concrete false estimate immediately upstream of the destructive sky-sent ḥusbān.
terra: The garden owner doubts the Hour and expects an even better return, extending the false estimate that the sky-sent ḥusbān overturns.
terra: His companion asks أَكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ, naming disbelief toward the Creator within the very passage where the ḥusbān destroys presumed security.
terra: لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ is what the garden owner should have acknowledged before the threatened ḥusbān; it directly corrects the 90:5 supposition that no one has power over him.

luna: The source dictionary’s root ḥ-s-b links “he supposes” to a fire from the sky; this ayah uses حُسْبَانًا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ for a calamity that burns up the garden. | terra: The threatened حُسْبَانًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ is the Quranic wording behind the source section's dictionary gloss “a fire from heaven that burns it,” giving the ح س ب family its destructive-fire sense.
terra: The man's fruit is encompassed and he wrings his hands over what he spent after the threatened ḥusbān, showing the ruin produced by the source section's “fire from heaven” gloss.
terra: He has no party to help him apart from God and cannot defend himself, answering the delusion of secure power that precedes the section's enclosing fire.
luna: The criminals see the Fire, expect to fall into it, and find no escape; this joins the section’s seen-from-afar fire to its final image of enclosure.
terra: Hell is displayed openly to the disbelievers, reversing the hidden or unperceived fire before 18:101 explains the covering over their eyes.
terra: Their eyes had been فِي غِطَاءٍ عَن ذِكْرِي and they could not hear; a covering over perception explains why the warning displayed in 18:100 had not guided them.

luna: This ayah introduces the story of Moses with a divine question; 20:10 supplies the actual distant-fire scene that the question opens. | terra: The divine question asking whether Moses' report has reached the addressee frames the fire scene as a transmitted reminder; 20:10 supplies the fire itself.

luna: The ayah brings together seeing, ānastu (ءَانَسْتُ), a fire, and seeking guidance by it (هُدًۭى), exactly the meeting of roots and scene developed in the section. | terra: Moses sees a distant fire, says آنَسْتُ نَارًا, and hopes to find هُدًى at it; sight, the section's ء ن س sense, fire, and road-guidance meet in one ayah.

luna: After Moses comes to the fire, this ayah says he is called; it continues the scene and shows the fire as the setting for divine guidance. | terra: When Moses reaches the fire, فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَىٰ; the far-seen marker actually becomes an address, beginning the guidance he hoped to find in 20:10.
terra: The voice at the reached fire identifies the sacred valley of Tuwa, showing that the distant fire has led Moses to a marked sacred place.
terra: At the fire God says He has chosen Moses and commands him to listen to revelation, supplying the concrete guidance anticipated in 20:10.
terra: At the reached fire God identifies Himself and commands worship and prayer for remembrance, giving concrete content to the guidance Moses hoped to find there.
luna: This ayah says God made roads in the earth so people may be guided, another explicit road-and-guidance formulation alongside the section’s beacon and the roadways in 16:15 and 43:10.
terra: Whoever follows God's guidance will neither go astray nor suffer, stating the safe course whose concrete emblem in 20:10 was the distant fire.
terra: Turning away from God's reminder yields constricted life and resurrection blind, reversing both the useful reminder-fire and the sight by which it is followed.
terra: The resurrected person asks why he has been raised blind although he once saw, foregrounding the failed use and eventual loss of sight.
terra: God answers that His signs came but were forgotten, so the person is forgotten that Day; ignored guidance explains the blindness of 20:124-125.

luna: God makes mountain pathways so people may be guided, a physical route parallel to the section’s high route-marker. | terra: Mountain passes are made as roads لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ, joining elevated terrain, a traversable way, and guidance.
terra: The persecutors command one another to burn Abraham and support their gods, supplying the human punitive intention that God's command to the fire reverses in 21:69.
terra: God commands the fire to be coolness and safety for Abraham; fire that would imprison and burn becomes, by divine speech, a place of rescue.
terra: Garments of fire are cut for the disputants, turning fire into clothing that surrounds the body instead of a beacon outside it.
terra: Whenever they try to leave it from anguish they are returned to it, staging repeated failed escape from the enclosing fire.
terra: Travel through the land should produce hearts that understand and ears that hear; the true blindness is in hearts, joining journey, perception, and the heart reached by fire in 104:7.
terra: The people in punishment ask their Lord to bring them out and promise not to return to wrongdoing, directly voicing a desired exit.
terra: God orders them to remain despised in it and not speak, closing the requested exit of 23:107.

luna: The parable joins light (نُور) to a lamp kindled by a tree, whose oil nearly shines even without fire; it develops the section’s root link between fire and illumination. | terra: The lamp shines in a niche, its oil almost glowing before fire touches it, and نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ culminates in God's guidance to His light; illumination, fire, and guidance are explicitly joined.

luna: The ayah depicts layered darkness in the deep sea, with no light for the person God has left without light; it is a specific absence-of-illumination counterpart to the fire named for light. | terra: Layered darkness leaves a person barely able to see his own hand, and whoever receives no نُور from God has no light; it is the full absence of the section's guiding illumination.

luna: The section’s traveler sees a distant fire as guidance; here the fire sees its deniers from a distant place and roars at them, reversing who sees whom and what the fire does. | terra: The direction of distant sight is reversed: when the Blaze sees them مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ, they hear its rage; the far-off fire is no welcoming marker but an active threat.

luna: The next ayah confines the deniers in a narrow place, chained together; it adds an explicit cramped enclosure to the fire that sees them from afar in 25:12. | terra: They are thrown bound into a ضَيِّقًا, a narrow place of the fire seen from afar in 25:12; the distant threat closes into physical confinement.

luna: Night is made a garment and sleep a rest, with day as rising again; it joins the section’s covering night and the dictionary sense of fire as a place to rest. | terra: God makes night a garment and sleep repose, then makes day a rising; covering darkness and rest meet in one formulation behind the section's night-side fire.
terra: The servants ask their Lord to turn Hell's punishment away because its torment is inseparable; prayer marks the boundary before fire becomes one's abode.
terra: Hell is an evil مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا, reversing the source section's secondary idea of fire as something beside which one rests.

luna: The ayah has Moses say ānastu (ءَانَسْتُ) when he notices a fire and promises a brand or news, with warmth as its use (تَصْطَلُونَ). | terra: Moses says آنَسْتُ نَارًا and offers to return with news or a burning brand so his family may warm themselves, joining distant perception to fire as sheltering utility.

luna: This ayah continues the fire scene: when Moses reaches it, he is called and the place is blessed; it adds the transition from finding a fire to receiving a call. | terra: On reaching the fire Moses is called and those in and around it are blessed; the apparently ordinary warming fire opens into a divine encounter.

luna: The next ayah identifies the caller as Allah addressing Moses; it completes the divine call begun at the fire in 27:8. | terra: The voice at the fire identifies its speaker as God, the Mighty and Wise, completing the transition from a perceived roadside fire to revelation.

luna: The question asks who guides people in the darknesses of land and sea and sends winds as good news; it joins night guidance with a sign before mercy. | terra: The rhetorical question asks who guides people through the darknesses of land and sea, placing guidance precisely in the travel-darkness where the section's fire appears.

luna: The ayah pairs night as a place to rest (لِيَسْكُنُوا۟ فِيهِ) with day made visible, echoing the section’s linked rest, night, and sight. | terra: Night is made so people may rest in it and day is made giving sight, pairing س ك ن with visibility in the same contrast that the night fire resolves.

luna: Moses notices a fire at the side of the Mount (آنَسَ ... نَارًا) and hopes to bring news or a burning brand to warm his family, another direct version of the section’s scene. | terra: The fire is perceived with ءَانَسَ beside the Mount, then approached for news or a brand for warmth; this is the section's night traveler, high-place fire, sight, and rest scene.

luna: When Moses reaches the fire, this ayah says he is called from the blessed side of the valley; it continues the fire scene into revelation. | terra: When Moses comes to it, he is called from the tree in the blessed valley beside the Mount; the high-place fire proves to be the location of divine direction.
terra: If God made night continuous, no deity could bring light; the question exposes how indispensable a visible light is within travel-darkness.
terra: If day were continuous, no deity could bring night لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ; rest belongs to darkness even as the section's fire makes that darkness traversable.

luna: God makes night and day so people may rest in one and seek bounty in the other; this develops the rest sense of the source’s s-k-n dictionary note. | terra: Night is for rest and day for seeking bounty so that people may give thanks, completing the ordered alternation behind 28:71-72.
terra: Abraham's people propose burning him, but God saves him from the fire; one ayah turns intended fiery confinement into rescue and a sign.

luna: This ayah says Hell will encompass the disbelievers, a specific enclosure parallel to the fire closed over them in the section. | terra: وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ states that Hell already encompasses the disbelievers, joining the section's covering sense of disbelief to enclosing punishment.
terra: Punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, making the encompassing claim of 29:54 spatially explicit.
terra: كُلَّمَا أَرَادُوا أَن يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا أُعِيدُوا فِيهَا turns the section's sealed condition into a repeated action: every attempted exit ends inside again.
luna: The Messenger is called an illuminating lamp (سِرَاجًا مُّنِيرًا) and a caller to God; this joins light to guidance as the section does with a road beacon.
terra: Faces are turned about in the Fire while its people wish they had obeyed God and the Messenger; rejected direction becomes bodily exposure to flame.
terra: They say they obeyed leaders who led them away from the path, supplying the misdirection whose fire consequence appears in 33:66.
terra: The blind and the seeing are declared unequal, setting the perceptual boundary presupposed by a traveler who can or cannot discern the fire.
terra: Darknesses and light are declared unequal, the basic boundary reversed when a fire first illuminates and then becomes closed punishment.
terra: Shade and scorching heat are declared unequal; the useful sheltering side of fire cannot be confused with punitive burning.

luna: The disbelievers’ fire does not end in death or relief from punishment, extending the section’s closed fire into lasting confinement. | terra: The disbelievers' fire neither ends in death nor is lightened, making the closed destination temporally as well as spatially inescapable.

luna: Night is stripped from day and people are left in darkness; this makes the section’s hidden night and its seen fire into a concrete day-to-night transition. | terra: When daylight is stripped from night, people are suddenly in darkness; the scene isolates loss of illumination like the extinguished fire-light in 2:17.

luna: This ayah says God made fire from the green tree and people kindle it, another direct account of the fire whose root the section connects to illumination. | terra: God makes fire for people from the green tree, فَإِذَا أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ; fire's surprising created source makes it a sign rather than merely a human tool.
terra: A piercing flame pursues the one who snatches a hearing, giving an elevated visible flame a punitive rather than guiding function.

luna: The ayah says night wraps over day and day over night (يُكَوِّرُ); it gives a concrete covering image for the section’s night-etymology. | terra: يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ wraps night over day; darkness is pictured as a covering laid upon light.
terra: Layers of fire lie above and below them, and God uses that very scene to make His servants fear; enclosure and warning are one image.
terra: One whose breast God opens is upon light from his Lord, while hard hearts are in manifest error; received light and refusal divide into opposed conditions.
terra: The disbelievers are told to enter Hell's gates and remain there, making the gate a one-way boundary into lasting abode.

luna: The night is for rest and day is visible, another direct formulation of the rest-and-sight pairing surrounding the section’s night fire. | terra: God appoints night for rest and day for seeing; a fire that offers both repose and visibility becomes a compact meeting of the two gifts.

luna: The revelation is made a light by which God guides people and leads to a straight path, joining the section’s named light and guidance roots. | terra: Revelation is made نُورًا نَّهْدِي بِهِ, a light by which God guides; this states in nonmaterial terms the exact light-guidance relation embodied by the road fire.

luna: The ayah says God makes roads so people may be guided, a direct formulation of the wayfinding function assigned to the fire in the section. | terra: God makes سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ in the earth; it directly states the section's claim that the laid-out route serves guidance.
terra: The criminals remain perpetually in Hell's punishment, another formulation of the section's exitless closure.
terra: The punishment is not lightened and they are left in despair, specifying the unrelieved condition of the confinement in 43:74.
terra: God commands that every stubborn disbeliever be cast into Hell, beginning a short judgment scene whose next ayah names refusal of good.
terra: The person cast into Hell is a preventer of good, linking the fire sentence to obstruction of the good course.
terra: Hell answers God's question whether it is full by asking for more; like the calling Blaze of 70:17, fire is given a voice rather than remaining a passive destination.
terra: الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ uses the ح س ب family for precise celestial measure, a meaningful counter-sense to the source section's sky-sent destructive ḥusbān.
luna: The people on the left face scorching wind and boiling water, a reversal of the useful fire that lets a traveler rest.
luna: The next ayah adds the shade of black smoke to their punishment, continuing the reversal of a fire’s sheltering or resting use.
luna: The smoke is neither cool nor beneficial; this completes the reversal of the source’s dictionary sense of a fire one rests by.

luna: This ayah asks about the fire people kindle; it introduces the traveler’s useful fire described in 56:73. | terra: The Creator directly asks whether people have considered the fire they kindle, making ordinary human fire an object of divine interrogation.

luna: The next ayah asks whether people made the tree of that fire or God; it adds divine creation to the fire whose use 56:73 describes. | terra: The question أَأَنتُمْ أَنشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنشِئُونَ shifts attention from human ignition to God's creation of the fire's tree.

luna: The section describes a fire set to aid travelers; this ayah says God made fire a reminder and provision for travelers (مَتَٰعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ). | terra: God says He made that fire تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعًا: it both points beyond itself and serves its users, matching the section's fire as reminder and useful marker.
terra: God sends clear signs to bring people from darknesses into light, restating the directional work performed by illumination.

luna: The believers’ light runs before them and on their right as they proceed, a guiding light on the way that contrasts with the section’s fire shut over its occupants. | terra: Believers' light runs before them and on their right as they move toward their promised destination, an eschatological light that visibly guides its travelers.

luna: The next ayah has hypocrites ask for the believers’ light, then a barrier is placed between them; it gives a boundary between those with guiding light and those left outside. | terra: Hypocrites ask to take light from believers, then a wall with a gate divides inward mercy from outward punishment; sought light becomes an impassable boundary.
terra: The people outside the wall are told that false hopes deceived them until God's command came; this gives the self-deception behind their loss of guiding light.
terra: After the wall closes the division, their refuge is the Fire and no ransom is accepted, completing the movement from borrowed-light plea to inescapable destination.
terra: Neither wealth nor children avail their owners against God, and those owners are companions of the Fire, repeating the wealth-to-fire reversal.
terra: The repeated attempt to extinguish God's light and God's completion of it makes illumination an irrepressible guide despite rejection.
terra: Believers are commanded to protect themselves and their families from a fire guarded by stern angels; this supplies the punitive pole beside the light of 66:8.

luna: The believers’ light runs before them and on their right, a repeated image of light accompanying people as they move. | terra: The repentant move with their light before and beside them and ask God to perfect it, while 66:6 has just warned of fire; one divine illumination guides where the other fate burns.
terra: The nearest heaven's مَصَابِيح beautify it but are also made missiles against devils; an elevated light carries both visible-marker and punitive functions.
terra: Each group thrown into Hell is asked by its keepers whether a warner came, making ignored warning the immediate issue inside the fire scene.
terra: They admit that a warner came but they denied him, supplying the rejected guidance behind their acknowledgment in 67:10.
terra: The inhabitants of the Blaze say that if they had listened or reasoned they would not be among its companions; unheeded direction is what changed warning into punishment.
terra: When they see the promised punishment brought near, the disbelievers' faces are distressed; what was treated as remote becomes an immediate visible threat.
terra: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ is the condemned person's admission that wealth failed, and 69:31 then orders him into Hell.
terra: The command to seize and shackle the condemned person begins the physical enclosure that continues through Hell in 69:31 and the long chain in 69:32.
terra: ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ orders the condemned into Hell between the failure of wealth in 69:28 and the failure to urge feeding the poor in 69:34.
terra: The command to bind him in a chain of seventy cubits gives structural force to the confinement surrounding the fire sentence.
terra: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ names refusal to promote feeding the poor as a cause of the fire sentence in 69:31, linking that fire to the unchosen ascent of surah 90.

luna: The passage names لَظَىٰ, a blazing fire, a direct parallel to the sealed punishment in the section. | terra: كَلَّا إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ introduces the blazing fire that then strips, calls the one who turned away, and claims the hoarder.

luna: The next ayah says this fire strips the scalp; it adds what the fire does to the people it calls in 70:17. | terra: نَزَّاعَةً لِّلشَّوَىٰ gives the Blaze's bodily action before 70:17 makes it call its target; this is punitive flame rather than a distant useful light.

luna: The source section says the closed fire falls on those who reject God’s signs; this ayah says the fire calls those who turned away (أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ). | terra: The Blaze تَدْعُوا مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, so the fire itself calls the person who turned away from the right direction.

luna: The section connects the fire with people who hoard; this ayah identifies the called person as one who gathered wealth and kept it stored (جَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ). | terra: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ identifies the one called by the fire in 70:17 as the person who gathered and withheld wealth, matching the section's hoarder-to-fire movement.
terra: Those who submit تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا, deliberately seek right direction; this is the successful counterpart to the travelers who follow the guiding sign.
terra: The deviators become firewood for Hell, so the immediately preceding search for right direction divides from becoming fuel for fire.
terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ supplies another person who turns his back before 74:26 announces Saqar, paralleling the one called by the Blaze in 70:17.
terra: سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ gives the fire consequence of the turning and arrogance in 74:23.
luna: Saqar neither leaves nor spares anything; this gives the punitive fire an unrelenting force that reverses the section’s useful, resting fire.
luna: The next ayah says the fire scorches human skin; it specifies the bodily effect of the Saqar described in 74:28.
terra: إِنَّهَا لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ identifies Saqar as one of the greatest signs before 74:36 calls it a warning.
terra: نَذِيرًا لِّلْبَشَرِ makes the fire passage itself a warning to humanity, parallel to fire as تَذْكِرَة in 56:73.

luna: This ayah asks what brought people to Saqar; 74:43–47 give their answer, so it frames the following fire scene and its causes. | terra: The question مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ asks what course brought them into Saqar; 74:44 answers with failure to feed the needy.
luna: The people in Saqar say they were not among those who prayed; it supplies one cause of entry into the fire being asked about in 74:42.

luna: They say they did not feed the poor, a direct reversal of the section’s feeding of the needy and mercy before its closing fire. | terra: The people of Saqar confess وَكَانَ لَا نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ; failure to feed the needy is explicitly one road into the fire named in 74:42.
luna: They also say they joined in vain talk with those who indulged in it; this continues their account of the conduct leading to Saqar.

luna: They say they denied the Day of Judgment, a concrete instance of rejecting the signs before the fire in the section. | terra: The people of Saqar confess that they denied the Day of Judgment, another precise form of the denial that turns a warning into fire.
luna: Their denial lasted until certainty came; this completes the Saqar group’s answer about how they reached the fire.
terra: God guides the human being to the way, leaving a grateful or ungrateful response; the next ayah gives the ungrateful response its fire consequence.
terra: Chains, shackles, and a Blaze are prepared for the ungrateful, turning rejection of the shown way in 76:3 into both enclosure and fire.
luna: The shade offered in the fire scene gives no shade and cannot protect from the flame, reversing the section’s fire as a waymark and a place to rest by.
luna: The next ayah describes sparks cast from the flame like palaces; it continues the fire scene with a visible, outward-moving image.
luna: Sleep is made a rest (سُبَاتًا), a specific rest-language parallel to the source dictionary’s fire as something one rests by.

luna: The next ayah calls night a covering (لِبَاسًا), matching the source section’s account of night concealing by darkness. | terra: Night is made a garment, another compact Quranic statement of the darkness that covers what the road traveler must discern.
terra: Transgression begins the course whose destination is identified as Hell in 79:39.
terra: Preferring the nearer life specifies the choice that makes Hell the refuge in the next ayah.
terra: Hell is the refuge for the one who transgressed and preferred the nearer life, turning a chosen orientation into a final dwelling.
terra: The أصحاب الأخدود are identified by a fire full of fuel, establishing the trench-fire witnessed in the following ayat.
terra: The persecutors sit over the fuel-filled fire, a spatial reversal of fire closing over its inhabitants.
terra: They witness what they do to the believers, placing culpable human sight beside the fire and sharply answering the supposition that no one sees.
luna: This ayah says the orphan is not honored; it opens a passage that contrasts with the section’s uphill acts of care before its final fire.

luna: This ayah says people do not urge one another to feed the poor, a direct reversal of the section’s feeding and mercy before the companions of the Fire are named. | terra: Failure to urge feeding the poor is named before Hell is brought forward in 89:23, tying the visible fire to refusal of surah 90's ascent.

luna: The passage adds devouring inheritance greedily; it continues the contrast between the section’s care for the needy and the conduct associated with the later Fire. | terra: Consuming inheritance greedily adds a concrete misuse of property to the conduct judged when Hell is brought near.

luna: This ayah names excessive love of wealth, directly matching the section’s hoarder and the boast about amassed wealth in its surah. | terra: Excessive love of wealth completes the wealth-centered failure immediately before the judgment scene and the brought-near Hell.

luna: Here Hell is brought forth. Earlier in this surah, 89:17–20 names neglect of orphans and the poor and excessive love of wealth, dispositions that echo the section’s contrast between care and the sealed fire. | terra: Hell is brought forward and the human being finally remembers; the warning once available at a distance becomes present when remembrance is too late.

luna: The next ayah says no one punishes as God punishes on that day; it intensifies the judgment scene begun when Hell is brought forth in 89:23. | terra: After Hell is brought forward, no one punishes as God punishes; this reverses the human supposition that no one has power over him.

luna: The following ayah says none binds as God binds; this adds a specific confinement image to the Hell scene introduced in 89:23. | terra: No one binds as God binds, giving the enclosing consequence of the false confidence answered in 89:25.
luna: The day displays the sun; the next ayah gives the reversal of night covering it, matching the section’s contrast between visible fire and concealing night.

luna: The source section glosses night as covering by darkness; this ayah presents the night covering the sun, the direct opposite of a fire visible in darkness. | terra: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا makes night cover the sun, a concrete Quranic formulation of darkness hiding the light seen by a traveler.

luna: This surah begins with night as it covers, the darkness against which the warning fire in 92:14 is later heard. | terra: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ depicts night actively covering, directly illustrating the source section's statement that night “covers with its darkness.”
luna: The next oath turns to day as it appears; it completes the night-covering/daylight contrast before the same surah’s fire warning.
terra: The declaration that human efforts are diverse introduces the two opposed courses whose second end is the blazing fire of 92:14.
terra: Giving and being mindful of God begin the successful course, the specific behavioral opposite of the miserly self-sufficiency that leads toward the warning-fire.
terra: Affirming the finest promise is the opposite response to the denial in 92:9 and 92:16, marking the fork before fire.
terra: God eases the giver toward ease, the other destination set against being eased toward hardship and warned of flame.
terra: The second course begins with one who is miserly and deems himself self-sufficient, the stance that leads through 92:10 to the warning-fire of 92:14.
terra: His denial of الْحُسْنَىٰ specifies what “turning away” means before 92:14-16 name his fire.
terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ makes the rejected course itself a facilitation toward hardship, preparing the fire that marks its end.
terra: وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ joins useless wealth to the fall immediately before divine guidance and the blazing-fire warning.
terra: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ places God's responsibility for guidance directly before the fire-warning, making warning-fire part of the surah's two-course orientation.

luna: The warning “with a blazing fire” (نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ) is a direct parallel to the section’s fire closing the surah. | terra: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ makes blazing fire itself the announced warning after the surah's divided courses of action.

luna: This ayah says who will enter the warned fire—only the most wretched; 92:16 specifies that person’s denial and turning away. | terra: لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى identifies who enters the fire of 92:14 before 92:16 defines him as the denier who turns away.

luna: The ayah identifies the one who enters as the person who denied and turned away (كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ), echoing the section’s disbelievers under the sealed fire. | terra: The person entering that warning-fire is الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, specifically one who denies and turns away from the guidance set out before it.
luna: The most God-fearing are kept far from the fire, the opposite fate to the deniers under the section’s closed fire.
luna: The person who gives wealth to purify himself contrasts with the section’s hoarder and connects the fire to the surah’s call to give and show mercy.
luna: The giver has no favor to repay; this clarifies that the giving beside the fire-warning in 92:14–18 is not a reciprocal transaction.
luna: The giver seeks the face of his Most High Lord; this supplies the inward aim behind the charitable action contrasted with hoarding in the section.

luna: The section’s source list includes raʾā (رءي) in the claim that a person thinks no one sees him; this ayah asks whether he knows that God sees, directly answering that presumption. | terra: “Does he not know that God sees?” directly answers the arrogant supposition that no one sees, making divine sight the warning before seizure.
luna: The disbelievers are explicitly assigned to Hellfire and abide there; this directly parallels the section’s disbelievers under a sealed fire.
terra: The addressees will surely see Hellfire, reversing the earlier failure to perceive the warning before it becomes punishment.
terra: They will see it with the eye of certainty, making unavoidable direct sight the final counterpart to a distant sign that could once be followed.
terra: الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ identifies the possessor whose calculation and accumulation end in the closed fire of 104:8.
terra: The wealth-gatherer يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ; the same “he supposes” stance as 90:5 and 90:7 leads directly into the fire shut over him in 104:8.
terra: كَلَّا لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ overturns the hoarder's expectation by casting him into the Crusher later identified as God's kindled fire.

luna: This ayah identifies the enclosed punishment as “the Fire of Allah, kindled” (نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ), complementing the source section’s account of fire as created light and as judgment. | terra: نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ identifies the Crusher of 104:4 and the enclosing subject of 104:8 as God's kindled fire.

luna: The section contrasts a beacon seen from afar with punishment; this ayah says the fire reaches the hearts, showing its inward reach. | terra: The kindled fire تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ, rising over and reaching hearts; it turns upward-reaching flame into inward enclosure.

luna: The section’s source word muʾṣadah names a closed fire; this ayah repeats مُّؤْصَدَةٌۭ and says it is shut over them, turning the familiar light into an enclosure. | terra: Its إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُؤْصَدَةٌ repeats the section's decisive مُؤْصَدَةٌ image almost verbatim: the fire is shut over its people.

luna: The next ayah adds that the fire is in extended columns (عَمَدٍۢ مُّمَدَّدَةٍۭ); it extends the preceding claim that it is closed over them. | terra: فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ completes the مُؤْصَدَةٌ scene with extended columns, giving structural force to the shut enclosure named in 104:8.
terra: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ denies that wealth and gain can protect their owner immediately before his flaming fire.
terra: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ gives the fire consequence for the man whose wealth cannot avail him in 111:2.
